title: With boundary, counting maps into S3 is #P-hard
claim: For a connected plane multigraph G, the fin handlebody X_G (one handle per vertex and, for each edge, a thickened torus attached along a curve in the class a_u a_v^-1, the curves drawn disjointly from the plane drawing and its mirror image) is a compact orientable 3-manifold with pi1 = <a_u, t_e | [t_e, a_u a_v^-1]>, so its number of homomorphisms into a finite group H is the sum over y in H^V of the product over edges of |C_H(y_u y_v^-1)|. For H = S3, repeating every edge k times gives an exponential polynomial in k with distinct nodes 6^a 3^b 2^c; interpolation from (m+1)(m+2)/2 values recovers the number of labellings with all edge differences rotations, which is 2 P(G,3). Since counting proper 3-colourings of planar graphs is #P-hard (Vertigan, cited), counting homomorphisms from compact orientable 3-manifold groups into S3 is #P-hard under polynomial-time Turing reductions (triangulating the handle description is standard, cited); for the dihedral group of order 8 the same argument recovers 2^|V| P(G,4).
failure_conditions: A plane multigraph whose brute-force homomorphism count of the presentation differs from the centralizer formula.
A plane multigraph where interpolation in k does not return twice the number of proper 3-colourings, or where the interpolation nodes collide.
foundation_claim_scope: Compact orientable 3-manifolds with boundary built from plane multigraphs; counting homomorphisms into S3 (and the dihedral group of order 8); Turing reductions; hardness of planar colouring and polynomial-time triangulation cited. No P versus NP claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py (standard library) compares the centralizer formula with brute-force homomorphism counts of the presentation, recovers 2 P(G,3) by interpolation on seven plane multigraphs (and 2^|V| P(G,4) for the dihedral group of order 8 on four), confirms distinct nodes and an extra value, and runs four controls. No human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with exhaustive finite checks
